description: S3 PACER node-local S3 cache. Panels are built only from metrics the daemon exports at /metrics (see crates/pacer-daemon/src/metrics.rs). RDMA copy-time panels are populated only on nodes running the efa-feature build with an active EFA transport.
title: S3 PACER — node cache

panels.description: Cache hit ratio = hits / (hits + misses). Cacheable GETs only; policy bypasses (small objects, no-cache) are excluded.
panels.title: Cache hit ratio

panels.description: Bytes served to clients from the local cache (pacer_bytes_from_cache_total). This is the client-facing cached-read throughput.
panels.title: Read throughput (bytes/s)

panels.description: S3 operations handled by the daemon, by operation name (pacer_ops_total, op label).
panels.title: S3 operations/s by op

panels.description: Bytes landing in client memory, counted AS EACH CHUNK LANDS (pacer_delivery_chunk_bytes_total). Use this and not pacer_delivery_bytes_total, which advances once per REQUEST when a span's last window lands: rate() over that measures completions bunching and reported 53.6 GiB/s on a single ~11 GiB/s rail (2026-08-24). Caveat that no panel can fix: a scrape interval coarser than the arm cannot show its peak — a 7-second checkpoint restore read at a 15 s interval is an average by construction.
panels.title: Delivered bandwidth (bytes/s)

panels.description: Chunk deliveries by where the bytes came from. peer_rdma is the only source that touches no bytes on this node; a rising peer_stream share means holders are declining to WRITE, which is a fallback to investigate rather than a failure.
panels.title: Delivered chunks/s by source

panels.description: Header-only 200s answered by delivering into client memory, against targets refused. Only reason=quota degraded to a body; malformed and unusable were answered with a 4xx and are client-side bugs.
panels.title: Delivery requests & rejects/s

panels.description: ADR-0030 point 2's first-contact race being absorbed or lost. A client must hold an address handle for the writer before a WRITE lands, and until its pump has built one the WRITE completes UNKNOWN_PEER. Retries with NO declines is the healthy shape. A decline means one chunk gave up and, because run_delivery is all-or-nothing, the whole GET degraded to a body.
panels.title: Announce race: retries & declines/s

panels.description: Fraction of object GETs answered by delivery rather than a body — the denominator for every claim the accelerated path makes. NaN with no GET traffic.
panels.title: Delivered share of GETs

panels.description: Pinned client bytes and registrations performed. On an ADR-0030 token window BOTH should stay at zero: the client registered its own memory, so the daemon names the window rather than holding it. A registration rate that tracks requests means the laziness regressed; pinned bytes at PACER_DELIVERY_PINNED_BYTES_MAX explains a rising rejects{reason="quota"} directly.
panels.title: Client pinning & registrations

panels.description: Payload bytes each rail has WRITTEN, from pacer_rdma_rail{metric="write_bytes_total"}. Covers BOTH peer serves and client deliveries (delivery joined this series on 2026-08-24, its depth and timing on 2026-08-25). This is the panel that answers 'did the WRITEs spread over the rails at all?' — one rail carrying everything is the source-pairing mistake that cost 30-60 % (a hash of (qpn, gid) put all 8440 writes of a 70B checkpoint on rail 7).
panels.title: Per-rail WRITE bandwidth (bytes/s)

panels.description: Pipeline depth: WRITEs posted on a rail and not yet completed. With the mean completion wait below this is Little's law — depth ÷ hold time is the rate a rail can sustain, and it is what separates 'the fabric is the wall' from 'the pipe was never full'. Pinned at PACER_RDMA_RAIL_WINDOW means the window is the binding constraint. The second series is the same quantity WITHOUT sampling aliasing: seconds of wire wait accumulated per second IS the time-averaged number of WRITEs in flight (Little's law), so it survives a scrape interval coarser than the transfer, which the instantaneous per-rail gauge does not.
panels.title: WRITEs in flight per rail

panels.description: Holder-arena ranges leased ÷ ranges the rail has. This is the pool EVERY WRITE whose source is not an ADR-0028 slab frame must lease and memcpy into, and a 32-rail node divides HOLDER_ARENA_RANGES (256) by its rail count — 8 ranges, 128 MiB in flight per rail at a 16 MiB chunk. Pinned at 1.0 says the SOURCE side is what a delivery is queueing on, not the fabric: enable the slab (cluster.cacheSlabBytes) so cached frames are written in place, or raise the pool.

targets.expr: sum by (rail) (pacer_rdma_rail{instance=~"$instance", metric="staging_in_use"}) / clamp_min(sum by (rail) (pacer_rdma_rail{instance=~"$instance", metric="staging_ranges"}), 1e-9)

panels.title: Staging pool occupancy per rail

panels.description: Seconds a WRITE spends on the wire, per completed WRITE: rate(pacer_rdma_write_completion_wait_seconds_total) ÷ rate(writes_total). Wall clock, not CPU — the daemon is asleep for it. Elevated here with post-batch time flat is the signal that a busy shared runtime is delaying the completion pump's wakeup rather than that the fabric is slow.
panels.title: Mean WRITE completion wait

panels.description: EFA rails the transport brought up at startup (pacer_rdma_rails): 1 on r8gd, 32 on p5.48xlarge. Fixed after startup, so a value below what the node exposes means the plane came up narrower than the hardware — the difference between a multi-rail run and a single-rail one silently.
panels.title: Rails up

panels.description: Completion-queue errors (each one marks a rail's RDMA plane unhealthy and falls the transport back to gRPC), plus the local buffers a WRITE still owns because no completion was reaped. Sources HELD is a live count that should return to zero between arms; sources ORPHANED rising means completions are being lost, and each orphan is a registered range that is never reused.
panels.title: Rail health: CQ errors & WRITE sources

panels.description: Cacheable GET outcomes: local hits vs misses vs policy bypass (pacer_cache_hits/misses/bypass_total).
panels.title: GET outcomes/s

panels.description: Cache fills: completed vs aborted (client disconnect or short read) — pacer_fills_completed/aborted_total.
panels.title: Cache fills/s

panels.description: Bytes written into the local cache (pacer_bytes_filled_total).
panels.title: Cache fill throughput

panels.description: Backend chunk reads that did not work first time. "retried" is a transient S3 fault PACER absorbed (pacer_backend_read_retries_total, one per retried attempt) — the client never saw it. "failed" is one PACER could not absorb, and every increment failed or truncated a client GET, which makes it the series to alert on: outcome=exhausted means the backend stayed unhealthy for the whole backoff window, outcome=permanent means a 4xx — this daemon's credentials or request shape, not the backend's health.
panels.title: Backend read retries & failures/s

panels.description: Fraction of peer serves delivered via one-sided RDMA WRITE rather than gRPC (pacer_peer_serves_rdma_total / pacer_peer_serves_total). ~1.0 = EFA path carried the load; 0 = clean gRPC baseline. NaN when there is no serve traffic.
panels.title: RDMA-served fraction

panels.description: Requester-side peer activity: fetches resolved from a peer, and fallbacks to a direct backend GET when a peer fetch failed (pacer_peer_fetches/fallbacks_total).
panels.title: Peer fetches & fallbacks/s

panels.description: Server-side peer activity: FetchBlob served, answered NOT_FOUND, owned misses read through to the backend, and peer-owned chunks admitted locally after the frequency gate (pacer_peer_serves/misses/readthroughs_total, pacer_local_admits_total).
panels.title: Peer serves, misses & admits/s

panels.description: Peer-to-peer byte movement, requester (from) and server (to) sides (pacer_bytes_from_peers_total, pacer_bytes_to_peers_total).
panels.title: Peer byte throughput

panels.description: RDMA serve-path bounce-copy time, holder and requester sides (pacer_rdma_holder_copy_seconds_total, pacer_rdma_requester_copy_seconds_total). ONLY populated on efa-feature builds with an active EFA transport; stays flat at 0 otherwise. Shown as CPU-seconds spent copying per second of wall-clock.
panels.title: RDMA copy time (efa builds only)

panels.description: Directory-shard RPC service time, in-lock op only, per op (pacer_dir_rpc_seconds histogram). p50/p99 across shards. The per-lookup CPU-cost input to the ADR-0020 activation decision.
panels.title: Directory RPC latency by op

panels.description: Directory RPC rate by op, from the histogram _count child series (pacer_dir_rpc_seconds_count). The op=lookup rate on the busiest node is the directory hotspot detector.
panels.title: Directory RPC rate by op

panels.description: Nodes in the current ring epoch (pacer_ring_members). Should equal the number of Ready daemon pods; a drop marks a membership change.
panels.title: Ring members

panels.description: Process CPU utilization derived from process_cpu_seconds_total (rate = CPU-seconds per wall-second ≈ cores in use). CPU-per-GiB is the RDMA path's headline win, so watch this against peer byte throughput.
panels.title: Daemon CPU (cores)

panels.description: RSS is what the cgroup limit acts on, and an OOM kill reaches no log — a 2026-08-21 restore killed the daemon (exit 137) with a routine directory sweep as its last line. in_use vs free_retained tells a retention bug in the daemon (find the owner) from glibc holding freed blocks on per-thread arena free lists (set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX, no rebuild). To get memory OUTSIDE the cache, subtract max(foyer_memory_usage, pacer_cache_slab_bytes) from RSS — never the sum, since occupied slab frames are counted by both.
panels.title: Daemon memory

panels.description: ADR-0028's payoff is the serve path posting a WRITE straight out of the cache, which only happens for chunks that got a slab frame. A heap-fallback rate that is not ~0 means the slab is undersized for the node's in-flight chunk count, and the pinned memory is being spent on a design that has quietly stopped applying — silent everywhere else, because throughput just looks like the pre-slab numbers.
panels.title: Cache slab (ADR-0028)
